thread:
incident-bot: Pager fired -> PD#P-78921: high GPU memory pressure in infer-west2a pool. 42 CUDA OOM events / min across 3 nodes. Severity: P1. nodes: gpu-rt-17,gpu-rt-18,gpu-rt-19. Autopath: throttle + route-fallback.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert sent to on-call rotation (kevin).

kevin: ack — I'm on it. seeing trace spikes in the last 6m. pulling logs now.

kevin: quick check - are any customer-facing endpoints returning 5xx? metrics dashboard shows a 2.3% error bump for text-generation-prod, latency +200ms for some traces.

sasha: @kevin thanks. If it's KV cache churn we should be able to drop prefixes. I'll prepare a drain plan.

maria: tagging customer-impact: a subset of Dedicated customers on infer-west2a might see timeouts. I'll open a rapid CS note if it persists >30m.

kevin: running command to drain most-loaded node: `reroute drain gpu-rt-17 --grace 30s --force=true`

incident-bot: Action logged: node gpu-rt-17 entering DRAIN (initiated by kevin).

kevin: drain started. also bumping fallback model replicas: `kubectl scale deploy/fallback-gen --replicas=3 -n runtime`

sasha: I pushed a KV cache eviction for large prefixes to free ~8GB on each node: `curl -XPOST https://ops/api/kvcache/evict?pattern=prompt-*`

pagerduty: Escalation policy triggered: notifying next-level oncall (sasha) in 2m if no resolution.

kevin: GPU OOM logs (excerpt): ```
[2024-11-02T14:02:11Z] cuda: out of memory allocating 1.2G
[2024-11-02T14:02:12Z] trace id=tx-9a3f ... kvcache miss spike
[2024-11-02T14:02:13Z] infer-runtime: fallback triggered for 12 reqs
```

maria: CS note: created ticket CS-4521, flagged customers A/B for monitoring.

sasha: after eviction see mem freed on gpu-rt-18: -6.8GB. rx error rate falling. continuing to monitor.

kevin: draining completed on gpu-rt-17, eviction + scale applied. routing restored to healthy pools. latency trending down.

incident-bot: Pager closed by kevin (acknowledged -> resolved) — auto-monitoring for 20m.

maria: I'll keep CS channel updated. If errors crop back up escalate to infra-sre.

sasha: +1 on post-incident follow-up: capture kvcache hit/miss trend, model batch sizes, and any long-tail requests that caused prefetch spikes.

kevin: short handoff: root cause likely prefetch + kvcache fragmentation during a traffic spike. mitigation: drain affected nodes, evict large prompt prefixes, and up fallback replicas. Next steps: schedule a deeper trace analysis and a runbook update. I'll paste a brief summary into #postmortems.

maria: marking incident as monitoring-> mitigated. filing customer followups.

kevin: thanks team. adding assignees: kevin (investigation), sasha (kvcache tuning), maria (customer comms).

sasha: copying useful logs into the incident doc. will follow up with quantized mem snapshot. :thumbsup:

kevin: closing thread here. will reopen if PD fires again.
